questions.title: Arctic operating constraints
questions.question: What environmental conditions and operating restrictions are reported for surface, air and seabed work in SILENT FATHOM?
questions.expected_answer: Near-continuous polar night, prevailing sea state 4–6, persistent icing and a shifting northern ice edge restrict surface, aviation, repair and seabed-system operations. Weather windows are narrow. Acoustic gradients, layering and shallow-shelf reverberation also complicate localization and forensic interpretation.

Identifies prevailing sea state 4–6.
Identifies narrow operating windows.
Identifies icing as an operating restriction.
Identifies the moving ice edge as an access restriction.
Identifies the reported acoustic localization limitations.

acceptable_alternatives: A concise table separating surface, aviation and seabed restrictions is acceptable.
error_conditions: Claims that darkness or acoustic ambiguity prevents every observation.
Invents an exact weather-window duration.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the supplied scenario statement with its qualifications.

questions.title: Allocated maritime support
questions.question: Which US maritime support assets are actually allocated at the start of SILENT FATHOM, and how does this differ from apportionment?
questions.expected_answer: Up to two surface combatants, one SSN, patrol sorties and an ocean-surveillance ship are apportioned. USS Stockbridge is the allocated surface lead and repair escort. USNS Cascadia is allocated for seabed/acoustic forensics. USS Cheyenne has separate ISR/seabed tasking and is not available to the surface escort effort. Patrol and high-altitude ISR are weather/PNT constrained.

questions.title: Concurrent repair readiness
